# restate_deployment (Resource)

A registered Restate service deployment: either an HTTP endpoint or an AWS Lambda function.

Registering a deployment performs **service discovery**: Restate calls the endpoint to learn which services and handlers it exposes. That call goes to your own infrastructure, so it can fail for reasons unrelated to Restate and can be slow; set `timeouts` accordingly.

Exactly one of `http` and `lambda` must be set. Switching between them replaces the deployment.

Deletion is destructive: the Admin API implements only forced deletion, which can put in-flight invocations into an unrecoverable state. `force_destroy` must be set before Terraform will destroy this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Registering a deployment performs service discovery: Restate calls the endpoint to learn which
# services and handlers it exposes. That call goes to your own infrastructure, so give it a timeout
# that matches how long your endpoint takes to become reachable and respond.

resource "restate_deployment" "orders" {
  http = {
    uri = "https://orders.internal.example.com:9080"

    # Sensitive, and preserved from configuration on refresh, so a value the API declines to echo
    # back cannot silently erase the configured credential.
    additional_headers = {
      "x-api-key" = var.orders_api_key
    }

    # Changing metadata replaces the deployment: the Admin API's update request cannot accept it.
    metadata = {
      team = "orders"
    }
  }

  # Deleting a deployment can leave in-flight invocations unrecoverable, and forced deletion is the
  # only mode the Admin API implements. Terraform refuses to destroy this resource until the flag is
  # set and applied.
  force_destroy = false

  timeouts {
    create = "10m"
    update = "10m"
  }
}

# A Cloud Run service, which authenticates callers with a Google-signed OIDC token.
resource "restate_deployment" "billing" {
  http = {
    uri = "https://billing-abc123-uc.a.run.app"

    auth = {
      google_id_token = {
        impersonate_service_account = "restate-invoker@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
      }
    }
  }
}

# An AWS Lambda function, invoked through a chained role. Pin the version: an unqualified ARN moves
# under Terraform, and Restate would keep invoking whatever discovery last saw.
resource "restate_deployment" "reports" {
  lambda = {
    arn             = "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:reports:3"
    assume_role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restate-invoke"
  }
}

# Discovery output. Terraform does not own it: re-registering the endpoint can change it.
output "discovered_services" {
  value = restate_deployment.orders.services
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `breaking` (Boolean) When registering, allow a service revision whose schema is incompatible with the previous one -- including a change of service type.

Like `force`, this is registration behaviour that the API does not report and that applies only when this resource is created.
- `force` (Boolean) When registering, override any existing deployment at the same URI or ARN. Implies `breaking`, and **can put in-flight invocations into an unrecoverable state**.

This is registration behaviour, not deployment state: the Admin API does not report it, so it cannot be read back. Changing it does not affect the existing deployment; it applies the next time this resource is created. The provider warns rather than silently ignoring the change.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Required before Terraform will destroy this deployment.

The Admin API implements only **forced** deletion. Deleting a deployment can leave in-flight invocations in an unrecoverable error state, so this has to be set deliberately -- and applied -- before a destroy will proceed.
- `http` (Attributes) An HTTP endpoint. Mutually exclusive with `lambda`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--http))
- `lambda` (Attributes) An AWS Lambda endpoint. Mutually exclusive with `http`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lambda))
- `overwrite` (Boolean) When updating, re-run discovery and replace the recorded schema information, **allowing breaking changes**.

Without it, an update moves the endpoint without rediscovering: the deployment keeps the services and handlers it was originally registered with. Set it when the endpoint's schema has genuinely changed and you accept the consequences.

This is update behaviour, not deployment state, and is not read back.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the deployment was registered.
- `endpoint_type` (String) Which endpoint kind this deployment is: `http` or `lambda`. Derived from the API response, which carries no discriminator of its own.
- `id` (String) Deployment ID assigned by Restate, for example `dp_1a2b3c`.
- `max_protocol_version` (Number) Highest service protocol version the endpoint's SDK supports, from discovery.
- `min_protocol_version` (Number) Lowest service protocol version the endpoint's SDK supports, from discovery.
- `sdk_version` (String) SDK version the endpoint reported during discovery, for example `typescript-1.9.0`. Empty when the SDK does not report one.
- `services` (Attributes List) Services this deployment exposes, as discovered. This is discovery output: Terraform does not own it, and re-registering the endpoint can change it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--services))

<a id="nestedatt--http"></a>
### Nested Schema for `http`

Required:

- `uri` (String) URI Restate uses to discover and invoke the deployment.

Optional:

- `additional_headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Headers added to every discover and invoke request. Typically API keys, so the whole map is treated as sensitive and is redacted from provider logs and diagnostics.

Values are preserved from configuration on refresh rather than being taken from the API, so a header the API declines to echo back cannot silently erase the configured credential. Adding, removing, or changing a header is applied in place.
- `auth` (Attributes) Per-deployment authentication.

Changing it **replaces** the deployment: the Admin API's update request does not accept authentication, so there is no way to change it in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--http--auth))
- `metadata` (Map of String) Free-form deployment metadata.

Changing it **replaces** the deployment: the Admin API's update request does not accept metadata.
- `use_http_11` (Boolean) Discover using a client that defaults to HTTP/1.1 instead of prior-knowledge HTTP/2. A deployment registered this way works only in request-response mode.

This value is **not read back**: the Admin API reports the negotiated `http_version`, and a TLS endpoint that advertises HTTP/2 over ALPN reports HTTP/2 even when HTTP/1.1 was requested. The provider therefore keeps the configured value and does not treat `http_version` as drift. Read `http_version` to see what was actually negotiated.

Read-Only:

- `http_version` (String) HTTP version Restate negotiated with the endpoint, for example `HTTP/2`. This is an outcome, not the read-back of `use_http_11`.
- `protocol_type` (String) Service protocol mode: `BidiStream` or `RequestResponse`.

<a id="nestedatt--http--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `http.auth`

Optional:

- `google_id_token` (Attributes) Have Restate mint a Google-signed OIDC ID token per request and send it as `X-Serverless-Authorization`. This is how a Cloud Run deployment authenticates Restate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--http--auth--google_id_token))

<a id="nestedatt--http--auth--google_id_token"></a>
### Nested Schema for `http.auth.google_id_token`

Optional:

- `audience` (String) Explicit OIDC `aud` claim. Omit to derive it from the deployment URI.
- `impersonate_service_account` (String) Service account to impersonate when minting the token. Omit to use Restate's ambient identity.




<a id="nestedatt--lambda"></a>
### Nested Schema for `lambda`

Required:

- `arn` (String) ARN Restate uses to discover and invoke the Lambda function.

Optional:

- `additional_headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Headers added to every discover and invoke request. Sensitive, and preserved from configuration on refresh; see the `http` variant for details.
- `assume_role_arn` (String) Role Restate assumes when invoking the function, for role chaining. Applied in place. Removing this attribute clears an existing role.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Free-form deployment metadata. Changing it **replaces** the deployment: the Admin API's update request does not accept metadata.

Read-Only:

- `compression` (String) Response compression Restate negotiated with the function, for example `Zstd`. Read-only: the Admin API reports it but accepts it on neither registration nor update, so it cannot be configured through this provider.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--services"></a>
### Nested Schema for `services`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Service name.
- `revision` (Number) Service revision this deployment exposes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The provider's admin_url already scopes the Admin API to one environment, so a bare deployment ID
# is enough.
#
# `force`, `breaking`, `overwrite` and `use_http_11` cannot be imported: the Admin API reports none
# of them. They are set to their defaults and the provider warns about it, so compare
# `terraform plan` against your configuration before applying. `force_destroy` is also false, so a
# destroy will refuse until you set it deliberately.
terraform import restate_deployment.orders dp_1a2b3c
```
